subject: LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: Verdict UNCHANGED after attack. I re-ran the two citations the record leans on and both hold, including the one most likely to have been inherited: the shipped COBOL0806 text cites 'ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F', and cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.1 'The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature' is OK while --check 8.8.1.4 on the same text FAILS - i.e. the diagnostic carries the CORRECT, one-level-deeper clause, which is the shape that is usually wrong. Annex F is confirmed 'Archaic and obsolete language element lists'. I also confirmed the non-support is sanctioned rather than chosen: Annex A carries 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor', so this is not a disposition the review is making and NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION is not warranted. No code implements the rule and its antecedent is unreachable on BOTH legs: (i) DataBinder rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with COBOL0806 at every edition that has the keyword; (ii) the standard decimal floating-point usages (3.167: float-decimal-16 and float-decimal-34) are rejected at the data description with COBOL1564. If either non-support is ever lifted, this rule must be written at the same time. EVIDENCE: 3.167 read verbatim: 'standard decimal floating-point usages / usages float-decimal-16 and float-decimal-34'. cite.py --check 15.58.3 on the rule-3 text: OK, rule 3. cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.1 'The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature': OK (General). cite.py --check 8.8.1.4 same text: FAIL. specs/ISO_COBOL.md Annex F heading: '(informative) / Archaic and obsolete language element lists'. Annex A processor-dependent item: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' DataBinder.cs: `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error("COBOL0806", ...)`. PictureAnalyzer.cs case "FLOAT-DECIMAL-16": `edition.Error("COBOL1564", ...)`. BindAlgebraicFold contains no arithmetic-mode test of any kind. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1). || editions 2014,2023 (kb/Work PB3173, S0b; DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §6 step 0): conditioned on standard-binary arithmetic, which the ARITHMETIC clause's STANDARD-BINARY phrase introduced at 2014; obsolete at 2023 but not removed (Annex F.2 item 3). cite.py --check 11.9.5.2 "If the STANDARD-BINARY phrase is specified" OK; cite.py --check F.2 "STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item" OK.
